Four snapshots, nineteen months end to end. In October 1948 the Nationalists hold most of China. By May 1950 they hold an island. Civil wars rarely end slowly — they end all at once.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Panel one, 28 October 1948. Communists hold Manchuria and a northern belt; the rest is blue. Days earlier the Liaoshen campaign had ended — 52 days of fighting that handed Lin Biao the entire northeast.

2/ Two more followed immediately. Huaihai opened against the Kuomintang headquarters at Xuzhou on 6 November 1948 and ran to 10 January 1949. Pingjin ran 29 November to 31 January. Together the three cost the Nationalists around 1.5 million veteran troops.
3/ Chiang Kai-shek resigned the presidency on 21 January 1949 and handed it to Li Zongren. The army was still nominally in the field. The state behind it had already stopped working.

4/ Panel two, 14 July 1949. The Yangtze was crossed on the night of 20 April. Nanjing, the capital, fell on 23 April against little resistance — a navy fleet and a river fortress had changed sides. Shanghai went on 27 May.
5/ Panel three, 28 October 1949. The People's Republic had been proclaimed four weeks before. What's left in blue is the southwest and the far west: territory rather than an army.

6/ Panel four, 10 May 1950. Hainan was assaulted on 16 April and declared taken on 1 May. The war didn't so much stop as run out of land that could be reached without a fleet — which is why Taiwan is still there.

7/ Notice what the mapmaker did: Tibet and East Turkestan are drawn apart in every panel. Both came under Beijing's control between 1949 and 1951. On a map of who holds what, that's a defensible choice and an arguable one.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
